sentence: The pasta was undercooked, drowning in some unholy gray sauce that tasted like someone had wrung out a dishrag into the bowl. The waiter rolled his eyes when I asked for water, as if hydration were a personal affront to him. I have eaten gas station hot dogs with more dignity than whatever insulting performance was happening in that kitchen. Forty-three dollars for the privilege of being condescended to by a man in a stained apron. Absolute disgrace.

I would rather chew on a wet napkin than ever step foot in that pretentious little hellhole again. The host treated my reservation like a hostage negotiation, the chef apparently thinks salt is a war crime, and the bill came with a smug little note thanking me for supporting local cuisine. Local cuisine? Local extortion is more like it. The only thing authentic about that place is the contempt the staff has for paying customers.

Whoever decided to put pineapple in the carbonara should be banned from kitchens for life. The bread was stale. The wine was vinegar. The owner came to the table and asked how everything was, and I had to bite my tongue so hard I tasted blood. This is the kind of restaurant that survives on tourist desperation and tripadvisor manipulation. A complete insult to the concept of hospitality.

Two hours waiting for a steak that arrived cold, gray, and apparently apologizing for its own existence. The manager had the gall to suggest I order something else and pay for both, like I was the one who'd done something wrong. I have never been so insulted by a piece of meat in my life. The whole place reeked of old grease and managerial incompetence. Burn it down and start over.

The brunch place charges twenty-eight dollars for two eggs and a wilted leaf, then has the audacity to add an automatic gratuity for service that consisted of slamming plates down and disappearing for forty minutes. The eggs were the color of disappointment. The toast was burnt offering. The owner stood by the door grinning like he'd just robbed me, because he had. Never again. Never, ever again.

I am genuinely furious that anyone gave this place a star, a recommendation, a passing thought. The risotto was glue. The salad had a bug in it. The bug had more personality than the entire waitstaff combined. When I complained, the manager shrugged and said that's how it comes, as if culinary mediocrity were a fixed law of physics. I want my money back and an apology in writing.

Calling that a burger is an insult to ground beef everywhere. It was a hockey puck on a soggy bun with a wilted leaf of something pretending to be lettuce. The fries were limp and salt-starved. The milkshake tasted like chalk. And the server had the nerve to ask if I wanted dessert, as if I would willingly submit to another round of culinary punishment from this overpriced cafeteria.

The whole vibe of that place is performative authenticity, like everyone working there read one book about Italian food and decided they were Marco Polo. The portions are insulting, the prices are criminal, and the chef came out at the end to explain his philosophy. I do not care about your philosophy. I care that my fish was raw in the middle and you charged me sixty dollars for it.

I have eaten in hospital cafeterias, prison waiting rooms, and a gas station in rural Idaho, and not one of those places served food as offensively bad as what came out of that kitchen. The pad thai was wet cardboard. The spring rolls were greased rubber. The dipping sauce was an act of aggression. Every single dish tasted like it was prepared by someone who hates eating and resents the customers for doing it.

What kind of sociopath charges fourteen dollars for a slice of toast with a smear of avocado on it? The cafe was packed with people pretending they weren't being robbed in broad daylight. The coffee was burnt sludge. The music was migraine-inducing. The barista misspelled my name on purpose, I'm convinced of it. I would sooner forage in a dumpster than give that place another dollar of my money.

If you cannot figure out how a four-way stop works after thirty years of having a license, you should not be on the road. You should be on a tricycle in your driveway, supervised. The guy in the white sedan today sat at the intersection for a full ten seconds with no one else around, then floored it through the stop sign as I was already halfway through. I hope his insurance premiums quadruple overnight.

Turn signals exist for a reason. They are not decorative lights. They are not a suggestion. They are not an admission of weakness. Use them, you absolute menaces. Every single morning I watch the same lane-drifting, mirror-ignoring, brake-stomping cretins weave through traffic like they're auditioning for a demolition derby, and somehow they all still have valid licenses. The DMV has failed us. The driving schools have failed us. I have given up on hoping.

I do not care how important your text message is. I do not care that your coffee spilled. I do not care about your sad story. When you drift into my lane at sixty miles an hour because you cannot be bothered to look up from your phone, you are a hazard, and you should be banned from driving forever. There is nothing more enraging than someone treating a two-ton machine like a personal lounge chair.

The pickup truck that tailgated me for six miles this morning had a bumper sticker about respecting the troops. I would like to inform him that nothing about driving four inches behind another car at seventy miles an hour respects anyone, least of all the people who fought so he could be alive to be this stupid. Back off. Just back off. You are not impressing anyone with your aggressive driving except other morons.

Merging is not a competitive sport. It is not a contest of wills. It is not a metaphor for your tortured masculinity. It is two lanes becoming one, a process so simple that every other species on earth could probably manage it, and yet here we are, watching grown adults play chicken at the on-ramp like absolute fools. The next person who refuses to let me merge gets nothing but pure, distilled contempt.

There is a special place in my list of grievances for the people who stop in the middle of an active travel lane to let someone out of a parking spot. You are not chivalrous. You are not kind. You are causing a six-car pile-up behind you because you cannot understand the concept of waiting two seconds. Drive. Just drive. Get out of my way and stop making everyone else suffer for your imaginary politeness.

Roundabouts are not optional. They are not negotiable. They are not a fascinating cultural artifact for you to study from a complete stop in the middle of one. The yield sign means yield to traffic in the circle, not freeze in terror while a line of cars piles up behind you. Every roundabout in this town has become a humiliating monument to public stupidity, and I am genuinely starting to lose my mind.

Slow drivers in the left lane are a societal cancer. I do not care if you think you are doing the speed limit. I do not care if you believe you are morally superior. Move. Get over. The left lane is for passing, not for your meandering tour of the interstate at fifty-five miles an hour with a line of forty cars behind you. You are not a traffic-calming device. You are an obstruction. Move.

The driver who cut across three lanes of traffic without signaling to make an exit they clearly saw coming for two miles deserves to have their license shredded in front of them. Did your mother not teach you to plan ahead? Did the driving instructor skip the entire chapter on lane awareness? I had to slam on my brakes so hard my coffee redecorated the dashboard, and you were already gone, blissfully unaware of the carnage you almost caused.

Stop honking at me at red lights, you absolute psychopath. I am stopped because the light is red. The law requires me to stop at red lights. You sitting behind me leaning on your horn does not change the color of the light, it only confirms that you are a small, angry person with no understanding of how traffic signals work. Have some patience. Read a book. Develop an inner life. Just stop honking.

After three hours on hold, I finally get a representative who tells me there is nothing she can do, as if she works for a charity instead of a multi-billion-dollar corporation that just stranded me in Cleveland for the night. Nothing she can do? Then what exactly is she there for? Decoration? You canceled my flight with no warning, no compensation, no apology, and now you want me to feel sorry for the agent reading from a script? Refund. Now.

Your bag fees are extortion, your seats are torture devices, your in-flight food is an insult, and your customer service is a black hole into which all reasonable requests disappear forever. I have flown on military transports with better hospitality. I have ridden Greyhound buses with more legroom. The next time I voluntarily board one of your planes, it will be because every other airline on earth has gone out of business and I have no other choice.

I was charged seventy dollars to check a bag that weighed exactly the same as the carry-on I was forced to gate-check for free because your overhead bins are designed for handbags and pity. Your business model is built on lying about prices and then ambushing customers at the counter with fees they had no way to anticipate. It is dishonest. It is predatory. It is the kind of behavior that makes me actively root for your bankruptcy.

Your gate agent looked me dead in the eye and lied about the reason for the delay. There was no weather. The pilot was not late. The plane was not undergoing maintenance. I watched the crew stand around chatting for forty minutes while two hundred passengers boiled in a jetway. The audacity of being lied to in person, by an employee paid to lie, while paying for the privilege, is genuinely staggering. Train your people or fire them.

I am writing to inform you that I will never, ever, under any circumstance, fly your airline again, and I will be telling everyone I know to avoid you at all costs. You lost my luggage for nine days. Nine days. With my medication in it. The representative I finally reached suggested I just go buy new toiletries, as if my prescription antidepressants were a tube of toothpaste. Disgraceful.

The seat in front of me reclined directly into my kneecap for the entire four-hour flight, and when I politely asked the man to put it up so I could eat the cardboard meal I had paid eighteen dollars for, he sneered and said the seat is designed to recline. Yes, into my body. Your seats are an engineering insult, your cabin layout is greed made physical, and the entire industry should be ashamed of what it has become.

Your app crashed during check-in. Your kiosk crashed at the airport. Your gate computer crashed during boarding. The only thing functioning reliably in your entire operation is the system that charges my credit card. Maybe invest some of those record profits into software that actually works instead of bonuses for the executives who designed this shambolic disaster of a travel experience. You should be embarrassed.

I have been a loyalty member for fifteen years. Fifteen years of putting up with your shrinking seats, your vanishing services, your rising fees. And when I needed a single flight change due to a family emergency, you charged me four hundred dollars and gave me a middle seat. That is not a relationship. That is a hostage situation. I am taking my business elsewhere, and I hope every other long-term customer does the same.

Telling a paying customer that their refund request will be processed in six to eight weeks is corporate cowardice. You took my money in two seconds, but returning it takes two months? Pure contempt for customers, dressed up in policy language. I want a human to look me in the digital eye and explain why a multi-billion-dollar company cannot process a refund as quickly as it processes a charge. The double standard is infuriating.

Boarding zones are a fiction you invented to make economy passengers feel inferior. By the time my zone seven is called, every overhead bin is full, every flight attendant is exhausted, and every chance of a peaceful flight has evaporated. The whole boarding process is a humiliation ritual designed to upsell premium seats. I see what you are doing. Everyone sees what you are doing. And we are all very tired of it.

Whoever designed this update should be banned from touching software for the rest of their career. The menus that worked perfectly for ten years have been buried under three layers of cryptic icons, the keyboard shortcuts have all been changed for no reason, and a chatbot now interrupts me every thirty seconds to ask if I need help. I do need help. I need help from the previous version, which you destroyed for absolutely no reason except boredom.

The application crashed three times in the last hour, each time losing twenty minutes of unsaved work, and when I clicked submit on the bug report, the bug report itself crashed. The level of contempt this software has for its users is breathtaking. It is not even hiding it anymore. It is openly hostile, and I am paying a monthly subscription for the privilege of being abused.

Why does opening a single document require accepting six dialogues, dismissing three popups, signing into two accounts, and waiting ninety seconds for the splash screen to finish congratulating itself? My document is forty kilobytes. My laptop has thirty-two gigabytes of RAM. There is no excuse for this. None. Software engineers used to make programs that worked. Now they make ad delivery platforms with a side feature of occasionally opening files.

I clicked on a setting to turn off notifications and was greeted by a five-step wizard, two upsell screens, a survey about my preferences, and a confirmation dialog asking me three times if I was really sure I wanted to do this. Yes. I am sure. I have been sure for ten minutes. I have lost the will to live in the time it has taken to silence your stupid pop-ups about features I never asked for.

Auto-correct just changed my colleague's name to something obscene for the fourth time today, and the option to add custom words is buried so deep in the settings I would need a sherpa to find it. The keyboard you ship with this device is actively undermining my professional life. Every email I send is a roll of the dice. I would rather type on a typewriter from 1962 than continue to fight this digital saboteur masquerading as a productivity tool.

Subscription software is a moral failure. I do not want to rent my word processor for the rest of my life. I want to buy it, own it, and use it without you reaching back into my wallet every thirty days. The fact that I can no longer open files I created with my own labor without paying you monthly tribute is theft dressed up as innovation, and I resent every single one of you who normalized this nightmare.

The search function in this app is genuinely worse than scrolling through every folder by hand. It cannot find files I just saved. It returns results from accounts I closed years ago. It ignores the exact phrase I typed in quotes. I have spent more time fighting your search than I would have spent organizing my files manually, and the whole point of using a computer was to avoid that. You have failed at the one thing you needed to do.

Every time I log in I am ambushed by a new feature I did not request, a tutorial I cannot dismiss, and an AI assistant that introduces itself like we are old friends. I am not your friend. I am a hostage. Stop redesigning the interface every three months for no reason. Stop hiding the close button. Stop pretending these changes are for the user when they are obviously for the engagement metrics on some executive's bonus dashboard.

I did not consent to the cloud. I did not ask for the cloud. The cloud is a marketing word for storing my files on a stranger's hard drive and charging me to access them. And now the app refuses to work offline, refuses to save locally by default, refuses to acknowledge that internet outages exist. When the wifi went down yesterday, I lost three hours of work that any normal program would have written safely to disk. Disgraceful design.

The terms of service for this update are eighty-two pages long, half of which exist solely to indemnify the company against the harms its own software causes. I have to agree before I can read my own emails. This is not a contract. It is a hostage note. And the option to disagree closes the program, locks me out of my account, and deletes my data. Pure corporate intimidation, dressed up in pop-up form.

I have asked you three times to stop reply-all-ing to threads that do not concern you, and yet here we are again, watching you weigh in on a project you are not on, were never invited to, and have no business commenting about. Read the room. Read the email chain. Read literally anything other than the sound of your own voice in your head telling you that everyone wants your unsolicited opinion. They do not. I do not. Stop.

When you took credit for the report I wrote during yesterday's meeting, in front of the entire leadership team, you crossed a line that I cannot pretend did not happen. I drafted every paragraph. I built every chart. You did not even read the document before you walked into that room and called it our work. We are not a we. Do not ever do that again. I am keeping receipts now.

Looping me in at the eleventh hour on a project that has been ongoing for six weeks, then demanding my input by end of day, is not collaboration. It is dumping. You did not plan, you did not communicate, and now you expect me to clean up the mess of your own poor management. I do not work for you. I work with you, and only because the org chart says so. Get your act together.

Per my last email. Per my last email. Per my last email. I am sending this for the fourth time because apparently the previous three did not penetrate whatever cloud of obliviousness you operate within. The deadline was Tuesday. It is now Friday. I am cc-ing your manager because the polite escalation has clearly failed, and I am no longer willing to absorb the consequences of your refusal to do your job.

I do not need a thirty-minute meeting to discuss something that could be resolved in a two-sentence email. Stop scheduling pointless calls. Stop demanding face time as if you are paid by the minute of meeting attendance. Some of us are trying to do actual work over here, and your incessant calendar invites are a productivity tax I refuse to keep paying. Decline. Decline. Decline.

Your habit of marking every email urgent and every meeting critical has rendered the words meaningless. Nothing you send is actually time-sensitive. Nothing you propose actually matters. You are crying wolf so loudly and so often that the entire department has tuned you out. The fact that you do not realize this, and continue to escalate, is genuinely embarrassing to watch. Calm down. Nothing is on fire.

I am not going to keep covering for your missed deadlines while you take long lunches and disappear from Slack for three hours at a time. The work is not getting done because you are not doing it. I am not your assistant. I am not your safety net. The next time something blows up because you ghosted a deliverable, I am letting it blow up, and I am pointing directly at the source.

The tone of your last message was so condescending that I had to read it three times to confirm I was not imagining it. I am not your intern. I am not your protege. I have been doing this longer than you have been at the company, and I do not need a junior analyst lecturing me about best practices in an industry he has been in for eight months. Step back. Way back.

You missed the deadline. Own it. Stop sending me elaborate explanations about how it was actually someone else's fault, the system was down, the data was unclear, your dog had surgery. I do not care. The deliverable was due yesterday. It is not in. Spare me the novel-length excuses and just send the work. Or do not send it, and accept the consequences like an adult.

If you forward me one more LinkedIn article about emotional intelligence in the workplace I am going to lose what little composure I have left. The irony of you, of all people, lecturing the team about empathy and active listening is so thick I could choke on it. Practice what you preach. Or better yet, stop preaching, because nobody asked, nobody is impressed, and we all see exactly who you are.

Three lanes closed for construction and not a single worker in sight. Not one. Not a hard hat, not a backhoe, not a guy holding a sign. Just orange cones stretching to the horizon and forty thousand cars crawling through at five miles an hour for absolutely no apparent reason. Whoever planned this should be put in stocks in the town square. The contempt for human time is staggering.

It is two o'clock on a Tuesday afternoon and I am parked on the highway. Parked. Not slow, not crawling, parked. There is no game, no event, no holiday, no excuse for this except the city's refusal to invest in infrastructure for forty years while real estate developers built thirty thousand new condos along the corridor. The whole system is broken and everyone responsible should be voted out.

I have lived through three lane reductions, two bridge closures, one phantom construction project that lasted four years, and now they are tearing up the same stretch of road they finished six months ago. Who is in charge of this? Are they actively trying to make commuters miserable? The answer must be yes, because there is no other rational explanation for the sustained assault on basic mobility this city has waged against its own residents.

The light at the top of the off-ramp turns green for exactly four seconds before turning red again, and there is a line of fifty cars trying to make it through. Whoever programmed this signal is either incompetent or sadistic. I sit through that light six times most mornings, watching the same green flash mock me from a hundred yards away, and slowly losing my will to participate in modern civilization.

Every single one of these intersections needs a roundabout, a traffic cop, or a controlled detonation. The four-way stop near the school is a daily mass casualty event waiting to happen. No one knows whose turn it is. No one cares. People just lurch forward in random order and pray. The city has known about this for ten years and done absolutely nothing. They are negligent and they should be held accountable.

Why are there school zones with twenty-five mile-per-hour limits active at eight o'clock at night? There is no school. There are no children. There is nothing but empty buildings and a speed trap waiting to ambush exhausted commuters. The cops sit in the parking lot every evening, lined up like vultures, waiting to fine people for driving the speed the road obviously wants to be driven at. Pathetic revenue grab.

An accident on the other side of the median has somehow brought my side of the freeway to a complete standstill. Why? What are you looking at? You cannot help. You will never help. You are just slowing down to gawk like an animal at a corpse, and dragging the productivity of an entire region down with you. Drive past. Drive past. Mind your own business and drive past.

The traffic app told me this route would save twenty minutes. It did not save twenty minutes. It led me down a one-lane road behind a tractor going twelve miles an hour, then dumped me onto a closed street, then routed me back onto the original highway one exit before where I started. The algorithm is gaslighting me. The whole concept of helpful navigation is a lie. I would rather get lost using a paper map than be misled by another smug little app.

I sat through four cycles of the same red light because the cross street had no one, no one, on it, and yet the timer kept telling me to wait. Modern traffic engineering is a humiliation. We can land probes on Mars but cannot get a light to turn green when there is nobody coming the other way. The wasted hours of human life at this single intersection alone are a moral crime.

The merging cones have been there since the first Bush administration. They are now a permanent feature of the landscape. Birds nest on them. Children grow up thinking traffic narrows from three lanes to one is just how roads work. The contractor finished the job a decade ago and then never came back to remove them. Whoever is responsible should be dragged out of retirement and made to lift each cone personally. With their bare hands.

Two hours of my life that I will never get back, set fire to by a director who clearly believes that loud noises and shaky cameras are substitutes for an actual story. The plot makes no sense. The characters are interchangeable. The dialogue sounds like it was generated by a malfunctioning chatbot with a thesaurus problem. Whoever greenlit this gibberish should be reassigned to mopping floors at the theater showing it, where they would at least be doing something useful.

The lead actor delivered every line with the emotional range of a cardboard cutout in a windstorm. The score swelled at moments that were not actually emotional, as if the composer was trying to bully the audience into feeling something. The final twist was telegraphed so heavily in the first ten minutes that I spent the rest of the film hoping I was wrong. I was not. This film is an insult to anyone who paid for it.

What a colossal waste of a hundred-fifty-million-dollar budget. The CGI looked like a video game from 2003. The sets were obviously plastic. The villain monologue went on for so long I lost track of why we were supposed to care. There are independent films made on a shoestring that look better, sound better, and mean more than this bloated, joyless, soulless piece of corporate sludge. Studios should be ashamed.

The film opens with a voiceover so condescending it might as well be a public service announcement, then proceeds to spend the next two hours explaining its own themes in case the audience is too stupid to keep up. We are not too stupid. We are insulted. Treat us like adults or do not invite us to the theater. The director's contempt for his own audience radiates off the screen in waves.

Every female character exists solely to be rescued, mourned, or kissed by a male character. It is twenty-five and the writing room apparently still has not been told. The romance has the chemistry of a damp paper towel. The comedy relies on the same tired stereotypes I thought we collectively retired a decade ago. The whole movie is a fossil pretending to be cutting-edge cinema. Embarrassing.

I do not understand the praise. I do not understand the awards. I do not understand the standing ovations at festivals. The emperor is naked and apparently I am the only one willing to say so. This film is a meandering, self-important slog dressed up in beautiful cinematography and mistaken for depth. There is nothing here. The themes are obvious. The acting is mannered. The ending is a shrug. Pure cinematic vanity.

This sequel has the energy of a contractual obligation that everyone involved resented from page one. The original cast is back, all looking visibly bored, reciting lines that sound like they were written by an algorithm fed every previous installment. The callbacks are not nostalgic, they are desperate. The plot reheats the same beats. The whole franchise has become a corpse being puppeted around for one more payday.

Three hours. Three. Hours. There is no story on earth that justifies three hours of indulgent close-ups, redundant flashbacks, and slow-motion shots of rain falling on the protagonist's brooding face. The editor was clearly afraid of the director, because no one with the authority to cut this thing in half spoke up. By the end I was actively rooting for the credits to roll. Mercy. Please. Just end.

The trailer promised a thriller. The film delivered a confused, meandering domestic drama with three explosions inserted at random intervals to remind us we were supposed to be on the edge of our seats. Bait and switch is fine in commerce. In cinema it is a crime against the audience. I want a refund and an apology from every studio executive who signed off on this marketing fraud.

The villain in this movie spends the entire runtime explaining his master plan, which turns out to make absolutely no sense when subjected to any logical scrutiny. Why kidnap the scientist if you already have the formula? Why blow up the dam if your goal is to flood the city you live in? The screenwriters did not think this through. The director did not care. And the producers banked on the audience being too distracted by explosions to notice.

Forty-five minutes on hold. Forty-five. I was transferred to three different departments, each one insisting they could not help me and the previous department had given me bad information. The hold music was the same six-second loop on infinite repeat. The pre-recorded voice kept thanking me for my patience as if patience were a renewable resource. By the time I got through to a human, I was so livid I could barely speak.

The agent kept reading from a script even when I had already addressed every point on it. I do not need to be told my call is important to you. If it were important to you, I would not have spent the better part of a Saturday afternoon shouting at an automated menu system. Words mean things. Stop using nice ones to paper over the cruel reality of what this experience actually is.

The chatbot insisted I was looking for the wrong department for thirty minutes before finally allowing me to type the word human, after which it told me a human would call me back within forty-eight hours. Forty-eight hours. To answer a question your website could not. Whoever decided this system was acceptable customer service should be fired and forced to use it themselves. I would pay good money to watch.

I have explained the same situation to four different representatives in the last week, and not one of them has the authority to actually do anything about it. They can apologize. They can sympathize. They cannot fix. The entire customer service apparatus exists to absorb anger and produce nothing in return. It is a containment field. It is a moral failure dressed up as a department.

Stop telling me my issue has been escalated. It has not been escalated. It has been moved from one queue to another queue where it will sit for another two weeks before someone with the same lack of authority looks at it and moves it again. The word escalated has lost all meaning. It now means abandoned. Just say abandoned. At least be honest about it.

The representative told me the system was down, then put me on hold for ten minutes, then came back and told me the system was still down, then suggested I try calling back later. There is no system. There is just a polite lie used to terminate calls when the agent has run out of script. I know the trick. Everyone knows the trick. And we are all too tired to keep pretending we believe it.

I asked to speak to a supervisor and was informed that no supervisor was available. None? Not one? In an entire call center of presumably hundreds of employees, no one in a position of authority happens to be on shift? The lie is so flimsy it would not survive contact with a curious child, and yet the company expects me to accept it. The contempt is breathtaking. The cynicism is corrosive.

Reading the same paragraph back to me from your website does not constitute customer service. I have already read the website. I am calling because the website did not help. If you cannot do anything beyond recite text I could read myself, what exactly is the point of this conversation? End it. Hang up. Save us both the energy of pretending this is productive when both of us know it is theater.

Every email reply takes seventy-two hours, every reply asks me a question I already answered in the original email, and every escalation sends me back to the start of the queue. The system is designed to wear me down until I give up and stop bothering you. I see what you are doing. I am not giving up. I will keep emailing every seventy-two hours for the rest of my natural life if I have to.

The agent had the absolute gall to suggest that the broken product was somehow my fault for using it incorrectly. I plugged it in. That was the entire interaction. There is no incorrect way to plug something into a wall socket. Your product caught fire, and you are blaming the victim. The audacity is so dense it forms its own gravity well. I am taking my complaint public and I am taking it loud.

I have read your entire post twice and I am still trying to understand how someone can be so confidently wrong about so many things in such a small number of sentences. Every single claim you made has been debunked publicly for years. Did you spend ten minutes researching this before you decided to inflict your opinion on a forum full of people who actually do this for a living? Sit down. Listen. Read. You have nothing to teach anyone here.

The way you started your reply with um, actually tells me everything I need to know about how this conversation is going to go. You are not correcting me. You are performing correction for the benefit of whoever is watching, in the hope that you might score a point. There is no point. There is no audience. There is just a bunch of strangers who have collectively decided you are exhausting and your contributions are not worth engaging with.

Your sources are a blog post from 2011, a video by some guy in his basement, and a tweet from an account with seventeen followers. That is not research. That is the digital equivalent of asking the loudest guy at the bar to settle an argument. Come back when you have something approaching legitimate evidence, or do not come back at all. The forum will be just fine without your contributions.

Imagine being so devoid of self-awareness that you log on to a forum dedicated to professional photographers and lecture them about exposure triangles because you watched one YouTube tutorial. The arrogance is staggering. Half the people you are condescending to have shot for magazines, taught classes, run studios. You should be reading their posts and taking notes, not correcting their grammar. Sit down before someone helps you sit down.

You have been wrong in this thread, and the previous thread, and the thread before that. Three for three. At some point the pattern stops being bad luck and starts being a deficiency. People are not piling on you. They are responding to a sustained campaign of misinformation that you keep refusing to acknowledge. Step away from the keyboard. Touch grass. Reconsider your relationship to confidence and accuracy.

Spare me the gotcha. You did not catch me in anything. You misread my post, replied to a strawman of your own creation, and then declared victory before anyone else had even seen it. This is not how arguments work. This is performance. You are arguing with a fictional opponent who agrees with you that I am wrong. The rest of us are over here, watching you flail at a ghost, and it is genuinely sad to watch.

Block me. Just block me. I would block you if I had not already decided that watching you embarrass yourself in real time was a strange form of public service. Every single post of yours reads like a parody account of a worse version of yourself. The mods should ban you not for being a troll but for lowering the average IQ of the entire subforum every time you post.

Calling everyone who disagrees with you a shill is not an argument. It is the last refuge of someone who has lost the argument and refuses to admit it. We are not paid by anyone. We just happen to know things about a topic you clearly do not. Disagreement is not a conspiracy. It is the natural consequence of being incorrect in a public space. Grow up. Learn. Or leave.

Your post has been edited four times, each edit moving the goalposts a little further from the original claim, which was already wrong. We can all see the edit history. The forum literally shows it. Stop pretending you said what you wish you had said. You said something embarrassing, you got called on it, and now you are trying to rewrite the past in real time. It is not working. We have eyes.

I do not have the time, energy, or patience to explain to you why your position is incoherent. Read literally any book on the subject. Read the wiki. Read the pinned posts at the top of this forum that exist specifically to address the question you keep asking. The rest of us already did the work. We owe you nothing. Stop demanding free tutoring as if your ignorance were our responsibility.

Three weeks. Three weeks I have been without hot water, and your maintenance guy has shown up exactly once, declared he needed a part, and vanished into the ether. I am paying full rent for a unit that does not have functioning plumbing. I am bathing at the gym. I am washing dishes in the sink with water boiled in an electric kettle. The next email I send is going through the housing court, and you can explain yourself to a judge.

You raised my rent by twelve percent and have not fixed a single thing in this apartment for two years. The window does not close. The kitchen drawer is held together with duct tape. There is a permanent water stain on the ceiling shaped like an angry face that I have come to consider a roommate. You collect the check on the first of the month and then ghost every email until the next first of the month. This is not management. This is extortion.

The mold in the bathroom has its own ZIP code at this point. I have been emailing you about it for six months. You sent someone to look at it once. He took a picture. He left. I have not heard from you since. Mold is a health issue. Mold is a legal issue. Mold is a thing I can take you to court over, and I am one more dismissive reply away from doing exactly that.

The walls in this building are so thin I can hear my neighbor's alarm clock through them, and yet you charge premium rent like this is some kind of luxury accommodation. The hallway light has been broken since January. The elevator is a death trap. The intercom dials a wrong number. You have collected hundreds of thousands of dollars from this building and reinvested approximately nothing back into the maintenance of it. Slumlord behavior with a designer aesthetic.

Withholding the security deposit because of normal wear and tear is illegal in this state, and you know it. The carpet in the hallway between two doorways got worn from people walking on it. That is not damage. That is the entire purpose of carpet. The fact that you tried to bill me for it tells me everything I need to know about how you operate, and I am taking the entire deposit back through small claims, with interest.

Entering my apartment without twenty-four hours of notice is a violation. I do not care if you wanted to show it to a prospective tenant. I do not care if you forgot to email me. I do not care that you own the building. My right to privacy is not optional. Walk in unannounced one more time and I am changing the locks and forwarding the police your way. Try me.

The heater has been broken since November. It is now February. I have been wearing a winter coat indoors for three months while you tell me the part is on order. The part has never been on order. The part does not exist. You are stalling because fixing the heater costs money and your business model is built on doing as little as possible while collecting as much as possible. I see you. The whole building sees you.

Your handyman shows up two hours late, does the job badly, leaves a mess, and you charge me for the inconvenience. That is not a service. That is a hostage situation in a workshop apron. I would rather fix things myself than continue to invite this person into my home to make problems worse and then bill me for the privilege. Find a new handyman or learn to use a wrench yourself.

I am keeping a folder. Every email. Every text. Every photo of the broken appliances and the leaking pipes and the cracked tile. Every receipt for repairs I had to pay for out of pocket because you refused to do your job. The folder is thick now. Very thick. When this lease ends, the folder is going to a tenant lawyer, and you are going to wish you had spent five minutes returning my calls.

You changed the policy on dogs without notifying any tenants. People who signed leases with their pets are now being told they have thirty days to find new homes for them. Are you out of your mind? You cannot unilaterally rewrite a lease. This is going to court. It is going to a journalist. It is going to every review site that will host the screenshots. You have miscalculated, and you are about to find out.

The fact that this show has been renewed for a fifth season tells me everything I need to know about the state of modern television. It is a meandering, plot-hole-riddled mess that recycles the same three character beats over and over while the writers congratulate themselves on subverting expectations. There are no expectations left to subvert. There is only the slow, dispiriting realization that no one in the writers room is being held to any standard whatsoever.

Every red carpet event has become an exercise in unbearable smugness, with celebrities pretending the dress they were paid to wear is a political statement, and journalists asking softball questions like they were granted an audience with the pope. The whole industry feeds on its own self-importance and expects the rest of us to applaud the performance. I will not applaud. I will turn off the broadcast and read a book instead.

Stop remaking every film from the eighties. We have seen them. They were fine the first time. Your reboot adds nothing except a coat of digital paint and the smug self-awareness of a screenwriter who thinks meta commentary is a substitute for an original idea. There are thousands of writers with original scripts in drawers. Read one of them. Hire one of them. Stop strip-mining nostalgia for a quick paycheck.

The discourse around this album is genuinely embarrassing. Critics are tripping over themselves to declare it a masterpiece because the artist is famous, but the songs are derivative, the production is bloated, and the lyrics read like a tenth-grade journal. The emperor has no clothes, and the entire music press is enthusiastically describing the cut of his invisible jacket. Have some standards. The audience certainly does, even if you do not.

The internet has decided that this minor celebrity scandal is the most important thing happening on the planet, and millions of otherwise intelligent adults are spending hours of their lives arguing about it with strangers. There are real things happening. There are real problems. The fact that we have collectively chosen to use our limited attention on this petty nonsense is a civilizational embarrassment.

Influencer culture has produced an entire generation of people who confuse attention with achievement. They have no skills, no expertise, no contributions to make to anything, and yet they are treated as authorities on health, finance, relationships, and politics. The platforms reward this. The audiences enable this. The whole arrangement is rotting the brain of the species and we are not even pretending to fight it anymore.

Whoever decided that every movie now needs a connected universe should be exiled from Hollywood. I do not want to watch eleven hours of setup for a payoff that is itself just setup for the next eleven hours. I want a story. With a beginning. And a middle. And an end. Not a franchise. Not a content delivery vehicle. A film. Like we used to make. Like adults used to enjoy.

Reality television has done more damage to the public's ability to communicate calmly than any other force I can think of. People now believe that shouting over each other, throwing drinks, and storming out of rooms is the normal way to handle disagreement. Three generations of viewers have absorbed this as the cultural default. It is corrosive. It is exhausting. And the producers laugh all the way to the bank while we burn down the social contract.

Awards shows have become so insufferable that I would rather have a root canal than sit through one. The hosts are unfunny. The acceptance speeches are political lectures. The musical numbers are designed by committee. The whole spectacle is industry self-congratulation broadcast to the public so we can be reminded how unimportant we are. Turn it off. Read something. Take a walk. Do anything else.

The fact that we now have a thirty-million-dollar movie marketing budget for a film that did not even hire a writer worth fifty thousand dollars tells you everything about the priorities of this industry. They will spend more on a single billboard than on the script the entire enterprise rests on. Then they wonder why audiences are losing interest. They are losing interest because everything you make is the same hollow, calculated nothing.

Four hundred pages of self-indulgent meandering, dressed up in the kind of prose that thinks it is profound when it is merely opaque. The narrator's inner monologue could have been condensed to a single chapter. The plot, such as it is, exists in the space between thoughts. By the time the protagonist finally has his epiphany at the end, I had stopped caring about him approximately three hundred pages earlier. A book to throw across the room.

Every female character in this novel is described first by her body and second by her hair, with personality coming a distant third if it comes at all. The author is a grown man writing in twenty-twenty-five and apparently has not noticed that the world has moved on. The dialogue is unbearable. The romance is implausible. The whole book reads like a fever dream from a writer who has been talking to no one but his agent for fifteen years.

The premise had so much potential. The execution is a humiliation. The author abandons every interesting thread within fifty pages, retreats into a meandering second act about the protagonist's relationship with his father, and then resolves the entire conflict offscreen between chapters forty and forty-one. I have read fan fiction with more structural integrity. I have written grocery lists with more coherent arcs. A genuine disappointment.

The marketing called this book a literary masterpiece. The marketing lied. The book is a baggy, pretentious, overwritten exercise in writerly vanity. Every chapter contains at least one sentence so purple it should be reported to color authorities. The metaphors come in herds. The adjectives are stacked like cordwood. Whoever edited this manuscript was either too intimidated or too lazy to do their job. The reader pays the price.

I do not understand the awards. I do not understand the laudatory reviews. I do not understand the book club discussions that have somehow turned this thin, joyless novel into a generational touchstone. The characters are flat. The dialogue is wooden. The themes are so heavily underlined that I expected highlighter on the page. There is no there there. The emperor is naked and the critics are too embarrassed to mention it.

The first twenty pages are unreadable. The next two hundred are merely tedious. The final hundred try to redeem the whole exercise with a twist that has been telegraphed since chapter two. The author thinks she is being clever. She is not being clever. She is being predictable while wearing the costume of cleverness, and the difference is obvious to anyone who has read more than three novels in their life. Pass.

The author's previous novels were sharp, funny, and economical. This one reads like he fired his editor, his agent, and possibly his entire reading group, and decided to publish his first draft as a statement of artistic freedom. The statement received. The artistic freedom is noted. The book is a mess. Go back to the editor. Go back to the structure. Go back to the discipline that made you worth reading in the first place.

Every supporting character exists solely as a sounding board for the protagonist's anguished introspection. They have no inner lives, no motivations, no purpose beyond reflecting the central figure's brilliance back at him. The novel is essentially a solipsistic monologue with occasional human furniture. By the end I wanted to write apology letters to the imaginary friends who were forced to share pages with this insufferable man. Tedious. Self-important. Forgettable.

The footnotes outnumber the actual narrative. The acknowledgments section is six pages long and mostly thanks the author's editor for putting up with him, which is the closest thing to honesty the entire book contains. The novel itself is a slog. The structure is incoherent. The prose alternates between purple and beige with no warning. I finished it because I had committed to reviewing it. I would not recommend that anyone else make the same mistake.

Three hundred pages of historical detail painstakingly researched and then dumped onto the page in giant unbroken paragraphs that read like a high school term paper. The author clearly loves the period. The author clearly does not love the reader. Knowing things is not the same as making a story interesting, and the inability to distinguish between the two has produced a book that doubles as a doorstop in both function and prose density.

Eight forms. I had to fill out eight forms to renew a license that the same office issued me five years ago. They already have my information. They already have my photograph. They have a literal database with my name in it. And yet here I am, in the same chair I sat in last time, copying the same information onto the same forms, while the same clerk stares at me with the same dead eyes. Why do we accept this?

The website tells me I need to bring three forms of identification. I bring three forms of identification. The clerk tells me one of them does not count. I ask which one would have counted. He says he cannot tell me, that depends on the situation. There is no situation. There is only the situation of me standing here, with my paperwork, trying to do the thing the website told me to do. The contempt for citizens is total.

Form A says I need to submit Form B. Form B says I need to submit Form C. Form C says I need to first complete Form A. I am stuck in a paperwork loop that some sadistic civil servant designed forty years ago and no one has bothered to fix because the people who would fix it work in the same building that produced it. The whole system needs to be burned down and rebuilt from scratch.

The office is open from nine to four, closed for lunch from twelve to one-thirty, closed on the second Tuesday of every month for staff training, closed on every federal and state holiday, and apparently closed at random intervals for reasons no one will explain to me. I have taken three days off work in the last month to come here, and each time I have arrived to find the doors locked and a sign apologizing for the inconvenience. This is not government. This is theater.

The agent demanded the original paper copy of a document the agency itself issued electronically. They have it. They sent it. I forwarded the email to her, in front of her, on her own screen. She still demanded a printed copy with an original signature. I am genuinely furious that the rules of this place have detached from the laws of physics, common sense, and the technological present. We do not live in 1973 anymore. Try to keep up.

The number I called from the website is no longer in service. The replacement number on the new website is for a different department. The voicemail at the correct department is full. The email address I finally found leads to an automated reply telling me to call the original number. I am running in concentric circles. I have aged visibly. My family has lost track of me. Whoever designed this system should be tried for crimes against time.

I was told to come back tomorrow. Tomorrow I was told to come back next week. Next week I was told that the policy had changed and the form I had spent a month preparing was no longer valid. Months of work erased by a memo no one bothered to publish. Hours of my life consumed by an institution that treats its own citizens like an inconvenience. I want my time back. I want it all back.

Why does it require six weeks to process a request that consists of a single yes-or-no decision based on information already in your possession? The same agencies that can mail me a tax bill within forty-eight hours of a missed deadline somehow cannot return a phone call about an open case within six months. The asymmetry is by design. The system works exactly as intended, and the intention is to wear citizens down.

The DMV has somehow gotten worse. I did not think it was possible. I was wrong. There is now an online appointment system that crashes every time you try to book an appointment, and an in-person walk-in line that the staff actively pretends not to see. The clerks rotate every fifteen minutes so that no one has to deal with the same angry citizen twice. Whoever ran this place into the ground deserves a special wing of municipal hell.

I have submitted the same application four times. Each submission has been returned with a different reason for rejection. The first reason no longer applies. The second reason was the agency's own mistake. The third reason was a typo in their reply email. The fourth reason is illegible. I am beginning to suspect that no one is reading these applications and the rejection notices are being generated by a malfunctioning printer in a basement no one has visited since 1986.

Listen up. This company has stolen money from at least six people I personally know, including me. They take your deposit, they string you along with vague promises about timelines, and then they disappear when it comes time to deliver. I have receipts. I have screenshots. I have testimonials from former employees who left because they could not stomach being part of the scam. Do not give them a dollar. Do not give them your phone number. Do not give them the time of day.

The owner of this gym threatened to sue me when I posted an honest review about the broken equipment. The threat itself proves the review was accurate, because no legitimate business owner would respond to a customer complaint with legal intimidation. Three thousand people saw the original post. Now three thousand people will see this one. And the next one. And every one I write until either the equipment gets fixed or the gym goes out of business. Your move.

Save your money. This contractor will quote you a fair price, take a fifty percent deposit, demolish half your kitchen, and then add forty thousand dollars of surprise costs before he will finish the job. Every neighbor on my block has the same story. He is well-known in the area for this exact tactic. The state licensing board has been notified, the better business bureau has been notified, and now you are being notified. Walk away. Run.

I am not the only one this happened to. There are seventeen of us in a group chat at this point, all reporting the same experience, all with the same screenshots of the same boilerplate apology email that promises a refund that never arrives. This is not a series of unfortunate incidents. This is a pattern. This is a business model. And I am going to make sure every potential customer searches the company name and finds this post sitting at the top of the results.

The clothing brand that promised ethical manufacturing has been buying from the same factories as fast fashion competitors. I have the documents. I have the supplier names. I have the photographs of the labels. Their entire marketing strategy is built on a lie they thought no one would investigate. Surprise. Someone did. And the long thread is going up tomorrow morning on every platform. Apologize now or apologize louder later.

Stop pretending you are a small family business when you have eleven locations, a private equity investor, and a marketing department staffed by twelve people. The family-owned-since aesthetic is a costume. The whole brand is a costume. And you are charging family-owned prices for corporate-margin products. The deception is offensive. Customers who care about supporting local should know exactly what they are actually supporting.

The CEO posted a tearful video on social media apologizing for the harassment scandals at his company. The harassment did not stop. The video was a PR exercise. We have multiple new reports from current employees, all corroborating that the culture has not changed and the executives accused of misconduct are still in place. The apology was a lie. The reforms were a lie. The company is exactly what it was, just with better media training.

The dentist office that charges thousands for procedures they later admit were unnecessary has now sued a former patient for posting a negative review. The negative review was true. The procedure was unnecessary. The lawsuit is a SLAPP designed to silence other patients. Well it is not going to work, because every single thing they do not want public is now public, and the local news has agreed to run the story next week.

Their refund policy is a maze designed to make you give up. The store credit comes with hidden restrictions. The return window is half what the website claims. The customer service representatives are trained to deny, deflect, and delay. After six weeks of escalation I finally got the refund, but I am not the lucky one. Most people gave up. Most people are still out their money. The whole operation is engineered to steal slowly enough that no one notices.

I worked at this company for three years and I am posting this on my way out the door because I cannot in good conscience let another candidate walk into that place blind. The pay is below market. The benefits are deceptive. The manager screams at people in front of clients. The HR department exists to protect the company from the employees. Do not apply. Do not interview. And if you are already there, get out while you still have your sanity.

If I hear that bass line one more time at one in the morning I am going to start banging on the wall with a baseball bat. We have asked. We have written notes. We have left voicemails. Every single weekend it is the same routine, the same throbbing wall, the same childish defiance from a thirty-five-year-old man who somehow has never learned what acceptable noise levels are. Grow up. Buy headphones. Move to the country if you cannot live with neighbors.

Your dog barks for six hours straight every single day while you are at work, and the fact that you cannot hear it does not mean it is not happening. The rest of the cul-de-sac can hear it. The mailman can hear it. The poor animal is clearly miserable, you are clearly negligent, and I am out of patience. Get a trainer. Get a sitter. Get rid of the dog. But stop pretending this is fine when it is so obviously, audibly not.

Park in your own driveway. There is plenty of room. There is so much room. And yet for some reason your son chooses to park his oversized truck directly in front of my mailbox every single day, blocking my access and forcing the mailman to skip me half the time. I have asked nicely. I have asked less nicely. The next conversation is going to be with the city about parking enforcement, and I hope his truck gets towed all the way to the next county.

Your leaf blower starts at seven in the morning on a Saturday and runs for ninety minutes. Ninety. Minutes. There are not that many leaves on the planet. There certainly are not that many on your yard. You are not removing leaves anymore, you are conducting an aggressive sonic ritual against the entire block. Some of us work nights. Some of us have children. Some of us are this close to losing it. Buy a rake.

Stop letting your cat into my garden. I have planted flowers there for three years and your cat has destroyed every single one. It digs them up. It uses my mulch as a litter box. It stalks the birds I feed. When I mentioned it to you, you laughed and said cats will be cats. Well, neighbors will be neighbors, and this one is about to install a sprinkler that triggers every time anything four-legged crosses the property line.

The hedge between our yards is on my property. Mine. Not negotiable. You do not get to trim it however you like and certainly do not get to spray it with whatever chemical product turned half of it brown last summer. The fact that you did this without asking, then denied it when I confronted you, is the kind of pettiness I did not think adults engaged in. The fence is going up. Higher than the hedge. Goodbye.

Your kids have been throwing balls into my yard every single afternoon for the last two weeks and then climbing my fence to retrieve them. Not asking. Climbing. They have broken three plants and trampled my vegetables. Either teach them some manners or buy them a backyard of their own, because mine is no longer available as a community sports field. I have stopped tossing the balls back. I am keeping them now.

I do not care what your contractor told you about property lines. I care what the survey says, and the survey is in my filing cabinet, and the survey says your new fence is twenty inches inside my yard. Move it back or I will move it back, and you can explain to the next set of contractors why they need to redo work that was illegal to begin with. The audacity of building on someone else's land and expecting them to just accept it.

Your security camera is pointed directly into my bedroom window. I do not need to know why you have it. I do not need to hear the explanation. I need it moved. Today. Otherwise I am calling the police and consulting a lawyer about privacy violations. The fact that you tried to deny it before I showed you the screenshot of your own publicly-shared feed tells me everything about your respect for the people who live next to you.

The trash you leave on your driveway is now a thriving ecosystem. There is a smell. The smell is on my porch. The flies have started visiting my kitchen. The HOA has been notified, the city has been notified, and if nothing changes by the end of next week, animal control is being notified too. Either clean it up or face fines and a public shame campaign on the neighborhood forum. Your choice. Make it fast.

Take me off your list. I have told you to take me off your list seventeen times. I am keeping a tally now. Each call from this number is added to the tally. The tally will be presented in court along with the federal Do Not Call complaint I have already filed against your company. Stop calling. Stop calling. Stop calling. I am not going to buy your product. I am not going to take a survey. I am not going to listen to your pitch.

Calling me at seven in the morning to ask if I want to switch my electricity provider is not a sales pitch. It is harassment. Do you have any idea how many people in this country work night shifts? Do you have any idea how many parents are trying to get their kids ready for school at this hour? No. Of course you do not. Because you are reading from a script written by someone who hates everyone, including you.

I do not have a car warranty. I have never had a car warranty. I do not own a car. I have explained this to every single one of you robotic vultures that has called me over the past eighteen months. Whatever list my number is on, it is wrong, and someone in your company should be paid to update it, although clearly no one is, because you keep calling, and I keep yelling, and we all keep wasting each other's lives.

Stop pretending to be the IRS. Stop pretending to be Microsoft tech support. Stop pretending to be my grandson stranded in Mexico. Whoever runs this scam operation should be shut down by every regulator in the country, and the people who work the phones should be deeply ashamed of what they do for a living. Find a different job. Any job. Sweep streets. Cleaning is dignified. This is not.

I asked you to stop using my name as if we are old friends. I asked you to identify your company. I asked you to confirm I am on a recorded line. You ignored all three requests and continued your pitch. That tells me everything I need to know about whether this is a legitimate business call or a predatory operation hoping to catch someone tired enough to give in. I am not tired enough. Hang up. Click. Goodbye.

Do not lecture me about the importance of your product when I have told you four times that I am not interested. I do not need to hear about the limited time offer. I do not need to hear about how this will save my family money. I do not need to hear another word from you. The audacity of arguing with someone in their own home, over a phone line they pay for, about a product they have already declined, is breathtaking.

I have logged thirty-two unsolicited calls from your company in the last month. Thirty-two. I have screenshots of all of them. I have the carrier records. I have the FCC complaint number assigned to my case. The next call you make to this number will be the basis for legal action, and I am genuinely excited about it. Bring it. I am ready. I have been waiting for someone to actually answer for this nightmare.

Your supervisor is not going to defend you. Your supervisor knows the script you are reading from is bordering on fraud. Your supervisor is just hoping you hit your quota before someone reports the whole operation. Find a different employer. Find one whose customers do not hang up on you with rage in their voices. This is not a career. This is a slow erosion of your soul one phone call at a time.

Speak up. I cannot hear your script over the sound of forty other voices in what is obviously a chaotic call center. Did your employer not provide soundproofing? Did they not invest in headsets? Or do they not care, because the entire enterprise is built on calling enough people that statistical luck will produce a few suckers regardless of how unprofessional the operation is? Click. Block. Forward to spam.

Do not call back. Do not transfer me. Do not have your manager call back. I do not want to hear from your company in any form, ever, again. The next call results in a formal complaint to my state attorney general. I have done my homework. I know the relevant statutes. I am not bluffing. The audacity of cold-calling people in twenty twenty-six should be a class C misdemeanor and I will work tirelessly to make it one.

A pile of garbage on the floor of a museum is not art. It is a pile of garbage. The fact that the curator wrote a six-paragraph wall plaque about how it interrogates contemporary consumerism does not change what it is. Anyone who tells you otherwise is selling you something, usually for six figures. The entire industry has become a money-laundering operation dressed up in academic prose, and the rest of us are expected to nod along.

I stood in front of a canvas painted entirely black for twenty minutes trying to understand why it was being praised as a meditation on absence. There was no meditation. There was a black square. A child with a brush could have produced it. The artist's statement was longer than the time I spent looking at the work, and it told me what I should be feeling, because the painting itself communicated nothing. Pure fraud.

The banana taped to the wall sold for one hundred and twenty thousand dollars. The banana. Taped. To the wall. Whoever bought it deserves to lose every cent of it, and whoever sold it should be barred from the art world for a generation. We have all collectively agreed to participate in an emperor's new clothes situation that has gone so far past parody it has come around to genuine sadness. Real artists are starving while this nonsense gets headlines.

Performance art has become an excuse for self-indulgent narcissism with no technical skill required. The artist sits in a chair and stares at people. That is the piece. That is the entire piece. The line of fawning critics wrapped around the block to experience this profound encounter. There was no encounter. There was a person sitting in a chair, and a great many fools convinced themselves it was meaningful so they would not feel left out of the discourse.

Real craft has been abandoned for ideas, and the ideas are usually banal. Anyone can have an idea. Few can paint. Few can sculpt. Few can compose. We have decided to celebrate the idea-havers and ignore the makers, and the result is gallery after gallery filled with text-heavy nothing while the museums that actually contain skilled work are dismissed as conservative. It is a generation-long collective tantrum and I am done pretending it is anything else.

The artist's statement is longer than the painting is wide. Inside it, the artist explains that the work explores the liminality of post-postmodern identity in a fragmented digital ecology. I have read the sentence three times and it still does not parse. The work itself is two splotches of beige paint. The disconnect between the words and the image is the entire grift. Without the words, no one would look twice. With them, museums pay millions.

I went to the new contemporary wing of the museum and walked out within ten minutes. There was a video of an artist eating soup. There was a room with a single fluorescent light. There was a wall labeled untitled. The whole space had been carved out of an old industrial building, and the old industrial building had more aesthetic value than anything anyone had bothered to install in it. Tear it down. Put something real back.

Stop telling me my opinion on contemporary art is wrong because I do not have an MFA. The art is being shown in a public museum, paid for in part by public funds, in a society where I am a member of the public. I am allowed to think it is terrible. The condescension from gallery staff when an ordinary person dares to express dislike is the exact reason this entire field is collapsing in on itself.

The artist sold a single nonexistent jpeg for sixty-nine million dollars and the auction house clapped like seals. We are in a tulip mania. We are in the middle of one of the most embarrassing speculative bubbles in art history. When it bursts, and it will burst, the people who bought into it will look in the mirror and have to ask themselves what they were thinking. The answer is they were not thinking. They were following each other off a cliff.

The curators have decided that beauty is reactionary, that skill is suspect, that representational work is bourgeois. The result is twenty years of galleries filled with deliberately ugly, deliberately incoherent, deliberately alienating work. They mistake provocation for substance. They mistake discomfort for depth. And the public has voted with its feet, walking away from the institutions that used to matter, because no one wants to spend a Saturday afternoon being lectured by drywall.

The scam call that pretended to be my elderly mother's pharmacy nearly tricked her into giving up her Medicare number. Nearly. Because I happened to walk in and hear what she was saying. The people who run these operations target the most vulnerable, the most isolated, the most trusting, and they sleep fine at night. Whatever circle of hell exists for those who prey on the elderly, I hope each of them has a reserved seat.

Phishing emails that impersonate banks should result in actual prison time, with no exceptions for the cybercrime gangs that operate out of jurisdictions where extradition is hard. Every senior who has lost their savings to one of these schemes deserves justice. The whole industry exists because law enforcement has decided it is too hard to prosecute, and the cost of that decision is measured in destroyed lives. Unacceptable.

The romance scammer that strung my coworker along for two years took her entire retirement savings before she figured out what was happening. He sent her photographs of someone he was not, told her stories about a future they would never have, and slowly drained her finances under the pretext of medical emergencies. That man is somewhere right now, doing the same thing to someone else. I would like to know his name.

Crypto fraud is just fraud. We do not need to invent a new word for it because the technology is novel. The people running the rugpulls and the pump-and-dumps are committing the same offenses that have been illegal for a century, and the fact that they hide behind a Discord server and a token launch should not exempt them from the law. Prosecute them. All of them. Down to the last anonymous wallet.

The fake tech support that appeared as a popup on my aunt's screen demanded six hundred dollars in gift cards to remove a virus that did not exist. She gave them the gift cards. Her bank could not reverse the transaction. The retailer could not reverse the transaction. The police filed a report and did nothing. Six hundred dollars of a fixed-income retiree's money, gone forever, and the perpetrators are still running the same scam tomorrow morning.

The advance fee scam keeps working because the scammers cast such a wide net that even a one percent response rate generates enormous profit. Every single person reading this knows about Nigerian princes. Everyone knows the lawyer holding millions for a long-lost relative is fake. And yet the emails keep coming, because somewhere out there, someone is still falling for it. I do not blame the victims. I blame the regulators who could shut this down and choose not to.

Whoever is running these grandparent scams has stripped my neighbor's mother of every cent she had saved for a nursing home. Her grandson is fine. He was never in trouble. He was never in Mexico. He was never arrested. The whole story was a script. The voice on the phone was an AI imitation. And she is now ninety-one years old, scared, and broke. I would happily testify against the people responsible. Loudly.

Every package delivery text that asks for a payment to release my package is a scam. Every email from the IRS demanding action is a scam. Every social media DM from someone claiming to be tech support is a scam. I have stopped trusting anything unsolicited, and I am furious that this is the world we live in. The criminals have ruined every normal channel of communication, and we accept it because we have collectively given up.

The deepfake scams targeting CEOs are a preview of what is coming for the rest of us. Already there are calls from people who sound exactly like family members asking for emergency wires. Already there are videos of executives saying things they never said. Already the trust foundation of modern communication is dissolving. And the response from the platforms enabling this is a polite shrug. Disgraceful.

The investment seminar disguised as a free financial planning workshop is a scam. The high-pressure sales pitch at the end of the free dinner is the scam. The hidden fees in the contract you signed before reading carefully are the scam. The whole industry of fleecing retirees out of their nest eggs is built on a thousand small deceptions, each one technically legal, all of them adding up to ruin. Regulators, where are you?

Every notification on my phone is a small theft of my attention by an algorithm designed by people who know exactly what they are doing. The engagement metrics. The infinite scroll. The carefully tuned outrage cycles. The whole apparatus is built to extract as many seconds of human consciousness as possible, and we have let them build it inside our pockets. I am genuinely furious at how willingly we surrendered.

The platform changed its terms of service last week, and buried in the legalese is a clause that grants them perpetual rights to train models on every photo I have ever uploaded. Every photo of my kids. Every family vacation. Every birthday party. I did not consent to this when I signed up fifteen years ago, and they cannot retroactively conjure consent by burying it in a forty-page document. This is theft. This is a class-action lawsuit waiting to happen.

I am not going through your stupid five-minute video for the answer to a question that could have been a sentence. The whole platform has trained creators to pad their content into bloated multi-minute episodes because the algorithm rewards watch time over usefulness. The result is endless yapping with the actual information buried at minute four-twelve, if it appears at all. I have lost so many hours to this nonsense.

The comments section is now ninety-five percent bots, five percent enraged humans, and zero percent anything resembling thoughtful conversation. Every post about anything attracts the same six insults from the same dozen accounts that all opened in 2024 and have never posted anything else. The platform knows this is happening. The platform does nothing about it. Because the bot engagement counts in the ad metrics, and the truth is just expensive.

The fact that we have allowed teenagers to grow up inside an attention slot machine designed by behavioral psychologists is going to be remembered as one of the worst collective decisions in modern history. The mental health data is catastrophic. The platform owners know it. They have known it for over a decade. They keep iterating to make the products more addictive, not less. And then they testify before Congress about how they are looking into it.

I have been shadowbanned for three months on a platform I use professionally. No explanation. No notification. Just a steady decline in reach and engagement until I figured out what was happening from a forum post. The appeals process is a black hole. The customer support is an automated email that thanks me for my patience. I am one of millions in the same situation, and the platform pretends none of us exist. Pure corporate indifference.

Engagement bait is not content. It is a manipulation, deliberately designed to provoke outrage so people will respond. And the platforms reward it. Every algorithmic boost given to the most divisive post in the feed is a small tax on the quality of public discourse. Multiply that by a billion users and you get the social fabric of the twenty-first century, which is to say, in tatters. Owners of these platforms should be held responsible.

Every single update makes the app worse. The button I used daily has been moved. The button I never use has been promoted to the front. The dark mode now looks like dirty pond water. The font has changed for no reason. The new logo is offensive to my eyes. Whoever is in charge of UX at this company should be relieved of duty, and the previous version of the app should be restored by court order if necessary.

Stop showing me ads for things I literally just bought. The whole point of the data harvesting was supposedly that the targeting would be useful. It is not useful. It is haunting. I bought one pair of shoes and now every platform on the internet shows me variations of those shoes for the next four months. Either build a better algorithm or stop pretending the surveillance has any benefit to the user. It does not.

The verification system that used to mean something has been sold to anyone with seven dollars and zero standards.
